# Resource: stripe_charge

A direct charge of a payment source, such as Stripe's test token `tok_visa`. Stripe's API deprecates direct charges in favour of payment intents, and a `stripe_payment_intent` makes a charge too. With `capture = false` the charge only authorizes the payment; set `captured = true` to capture it in full. Stripe releases an authorization that is not captured within 7 days. Only `description` and `metadata` change after creation.

~> A charge can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `captured`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete a charge; refund it with a `stripe_refund`. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the charge, fail at plan time. To stop managing a charge, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Authorizes 20.00 on Stripe's test card. Setting `captured = true` later captures it.
resource "stripe_charge" "deposit" {
  amount      = 2000
  currency    = "usd"
  source      = "tok_visa"
  capture     = false
  description = "Deposit"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) Amount intended to be collected by this payment. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `application_fee_amount` - (Optional) A fee in cents (or local equivalent) that will be applied to the charge and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made with an OAuth key or the `Stripe-Account` header in order to take an application fee. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/direct-charges#collect-fees). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `capture` - (Optional) Whether to immediately capture the charge. Defaults to `true`. When `false`, the charge issues an authorization (or pre-authorization), and will need to be [captured](https://docs.stripe.com/api#capture_charge) later. Uncaptured charges expire after a set number of days (7 by default). For more information, see the [authorizing charges and settling later](https://docs.stripe.com/charges/placing-a-hold) documentation. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `captured` - (Optional) If the charge was created without capturing, this Boolean represents whether it is still uncaptured or has since been captured. Possible values: `true`.
* `customer` - (Optional) The ID of an existing customer that will be charged in this request. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string which you can attach to a `Charge` object. It is displayed when in the web interface alongside the charge. Note that if you use Stripe to send automatic email receipts to your customers, your receipt emails will include the `description` of the charge(s) that they are describing.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `on_behalf_of` - (Optional) The Stripe account ID for which these funds are intended. You can specify the business of record as the connected account using the `on_behalf_of` attribute on the charge. For details, see [Creating Separate Charges and Transfers](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#settlement-merchant). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `receipt_email` - (Optional) The email address to which this charge's [receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/dashboard/receipts) will be sent. The receipt will not be sent until the charge is paid, and no receipts will be sent for test mode charges. If this charge is for a [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object), the email address specified here will override the customer's email address. If `receipt_email` is specified for a charge in live mode, a receipt will be sent regardless of your [email settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/emails). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `shipping` - (Optional) Shipping information for the charge. Helps prevent fraud on charges for physical goods. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`shipping`](#shipping) below.
* `source` - (Optional) A payment source to be charged. This can be the ID of a [card](https://docs.stripe.com/api#cards) (i.e., credit or debit card), a [bank account](https://docs.stripe.com/api#bank_accounts), a [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api#sources), a [token](https://docs.stripe.com/api#tokens), or a [connected account](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/account-debits#charging-a-connected-account). For certain sources---namely, [cards](https://docs.stripe.com/api#cards), [bank accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api#bank_accounts), and attached [sources](https://docs.stripe.com/api#sources)---you must also pass the ID of the associated customer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) For a non-card charge, text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see [the Statement Descriptor docs](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors). For a card charge, this value is ignored unless you don't specify a `statement_descriptor_suffix`, in which case this value is used as the suffix. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `statement_descriptor_suffix` - (Optional) Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's [statement descriptor prefix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#static) to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement. If the account has no prefix value, the suffix is concatenated to the account's statement descriptor. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `transfer_data` - (Optional) An optional dictionary including the account to automatically transfer to as part of a destination charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges) for details. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`transfer_data`](#transfer_data) below.
* `transfer_group` - (Optional) A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. For details, see [Grouping transactions](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

<a id="shipping"></a>
### `shipping`

The `shipping` attribute supports:

* `address` - (Required) See [`shipping.address`](#shipping.address) below.
* `carrier` - (Optional) The delivery service that shipped a physical product, such as Fedex, UPS, USPS, etc.
* `name` - (Required) Recipient name.
* `phone` - (Optional) Recipient phone (including extension).
* `tracking_number` - (Optional) The tracking number for a physical product, obtained from the delivery service. If multiple tracking numbers were generated for this purchase, please separate them with commas.

<a id="shipping.address"></a>
### `shipping.address`

The `shipping.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - (Optional) City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - (Optional) Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - (Optional) Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - (Optional) ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - (Optional) State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="transfer_data"></a>
### `transfer_data`

The `transfer_data` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) The amount transferred to the destination account, if specified. By default, the entire charge amount is transferred to the destination account.
* `description` - (Optional)
* `destination` - (Required) ID of an existing, connected Stripe account to transfer funds to if `transfer_data` was specified in the charge request.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `amount_captured` - Amount in cents (or local equivalent) captured (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial capture was made).
* `amount_refunded` - Amount in cents (or local equivalent) refunded (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial refund was issued).
* `application` - ID of the Connect application that created the charge.
* `application_fee` - The application fee (if any) for the charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/direct-charges#collect-fees) for details.
* `balance_transaction` - ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this charge on your account balance (not including refunds or disputes).
* `billing_details` - See [`billing_details`](#billing_details) below.
* `calculated_statement_descriptor` - The full statement descriptor that is passed to card networks, and that is displayed on your customers' credit card and bank statements. Allows you to see what the statement descriptor looks like after the static and dynamic portions are combined. This value only exists for card payments.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `disputed` - Whether the charge has been disputed.
* `failure_balance_transaction` - ID of the balance transaction that describes the reversal of the balance on your account due to payment failure.
* `failure_code` - Error code explaining reason for charge failure if available (see [the errors section](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) for a list of codes).
* `failure_message` - Message to user further explaining reason for charge failure if available.
* `fraud_details` - Information on fraud assessments for the charge. See [`fraud_details`](#fraud_details) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `outcome` - Details about whether the payment was accepted, and why. See [understanding declines](https://docs.stripe.com/declines) for details. See [`outcome`](#outcome) below.
* `paid` - `true` if the charge succeeded, or was successfully authorized for later capture.
* `payment_intent` - ID of the PaymentIntent associated with this charge, if one exists.
* `payment_method` - ID of the payment method used in this charge.
* `payment_method_details` - Details about the payment method at the time of the transaction. See [`payment_method_details`](#payment_method_details) below.
* `presentment_details` - See [`presentment_details`](#presentment_details) below.
* `radar_options` - Options to configure Radar. See [Radar Session](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/radar-session) for more information. See [`radar_options`](#radar_options) below.
* `receipt_number` - This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this charge. This attribute will be `null` until a receipt has been sent.
* `receipt_url` - This is the URL to view the receipt for this charge. The receipt is kept up-to-date to the latest state of the charge, including any refunds. If the charge is for an Invoice, the receipt will be stylized as an Invoice receipt.
* `refunded` - Whether the charge has been fully refunded. If the charge is only partially refunded, this attribute will still be false.
* `refunds` - A list of refunds that have been applied to the charge. See [`refunds`](#refunds) below.
* `review` - ID of the review associated with this charge if one exists.
* `source_transfer` - The transfer ID which created this charge. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges) for details.
* `status` - The status of the payment is either `succeeded`, `pending`, or `failed`. Possible values: `failed`, `pending`, `succeeded`.
* `transfer` - ID of the transfer to the `destination` account (only applicable if the charge was created using the `destination` parameter).

<a id="billing_details"></a>
### `billing_details`

The `billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - Billing address. See [`billing_details.address`](#billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.
* `phone` - Billing phone number (including extension).
* `tax_id` - Taxpayer identification number. Used only for transactions between LATAM buyers and non-LATAM sellers.

<a id="billing_details.address"></a>
### `billing_details.address`

The `billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="fraud_details"></a>
### `fraud_details`

The `fraud_details` attribute supports:

* `stripe_report` - Assessments from Stripe. If set, the value is `fraudulent`.
* `user_report` - Assessments reported by you. If set, possible values of are `safe` and `fraudulent`.

<a id="outcome"></a>
### `outcome`

The `outcome` attribute supports:

* `advice_code` - An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation on [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#retrying-issuer-declines). Possible values: `confirm_card_data`, `do_not_try_again`, `try_again_later`.
* `network_advice_code` - For charges declined by the network, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice returned by the network on how to proceed with an error.
* `network_decline_code` - For charges declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the charge failed.
* `network_status` - Possible values are `approved_by_network`, `declined_by_network`, `not_sent_to_network`, and `reversed_after_approval`. The value `reversed_after_approval` indicates the payment was [blocked by Stripe](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#blocked-payments) after bank authorization, and may temporarily appear as "pending" on a cardholder's statement.
* `reason` - An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation of the outcome's `type`. Charges blocked by Radar's default block rule have the value `highest_risk_level`. Charges placed in review by Radar's default review rule have the value `elevated_risk_level`. Charges blocked because the payment is unlikely to be authorized have the value `low_probability_of_authorization`. Charges authorized, blocked, or placed in review by custom rules have the value `rule`. See [understanding declines](https://docs.stripe.com/declines) for more details.
* `risk_level` - Stripe Radar's evaluation of the riskiness of the payment. Possible values for evaluated payments are `normal`, `elevated`, `highest`. For non-card payments, and card-based payments predating the public assignment of risk levels, this field will have the value `not_assessed`. In the event of an error in the evaluation, this field will have the value `unknown`. This field is only available with Radar.
* `risk_score` - Stripe Radar's evaluation of the riskiness of the payment. Possible values for evaluated payments are between 0 and 100. For non-card payments, card-based payments predating the public assignment of risk scores, or in the event of an error during evaluation, this field will not be present. This field is only available with Radar for Fraud Teams.
* `rule` - The ID of the Radar rule that matched the payment, if applicable.
* `seller_message` - A human-readable description of the outcome type and reason, designed for you (the recipient of the payment), not your customer.
* `type` - Possible values are `authorized`, `manual_review`, `issuer_declined`, `blocked`, and `invalid`. See [understanding declines](https://docs.stripe.com/declines) and [Radar reviews](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews) for details.

<a id="payment_method_details.ach_credit_transfer"></a>
### `payment_method_details.ach_credit_transfer`

The `payment_method_details.ach_credit_transfer` attribute supports:

* `account_number` - Account number to transfer funds to.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the routing number.
* `routing_number` - Routing transit number for the bank account to transfer funds to.
* `swift_code` - SWIFT code of the bank associated with the routing number.

<a id="payment_method_details.ach_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.ach_debit`

The `payment_method_details.ach_debit` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `routing_number` - Routing transit number of the bank account.

<a id="payment_method_details.acss_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.acss_debit`

The `payment_method_details.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `institution_number` - Institution number of the bank account
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `transit_number` - Transit number of the bank account.

<a id="payment_method_details.affirm"></a>
### `payment_method_details.affirm`

The `payment_method_details.affirm` attribute supports:

* `location` - ID of the location that this reader is assigned to.
* `reader` - ID of the reader this transaction was made on.
* `transaction_id` - The Affirm transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.afterpay_clearpay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.afterpay_clearpay`

The `payment_method_details.afterpay_clearpay` attribute supports:

* `order_id` - The Afterpay order ID associated with this payment intent.
* `reference` - Order identifier shown to the merchant in Afterpay's online portal.

<a id="payment_method_details.alipay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.alipay`

The `payment_method_details.alipay` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - Uniquely identifies this particular Alipay account. You can use this attribute to check whether two Alipay accounts are the same.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular Alipay account. You can use this attribute to check whether two Alipay accounts are the same.
* `transaction_id` - Transaction ID of this particular Alipay transaction.

### `payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding`

The `payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding` attribute supports:

* `card` - See [`payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card`](#payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card) below.
* `type` - funding type of the underlying payment method. Possible values: `card`.

<a id="payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card"></a>
### `payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card`

The `payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `American Express`, `Cartes Bancaires`, `Diners Club`, `Discover`, `Eftpos Australia`, `Girocard`, `JCB`, `MasterCard`, `UnionPay`, `Visa`, or `Unknown`.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.

<a id="payment_method_details.au_becs_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.au_becs_debit`

The `payment_method_details.au_becs_debit` attribute supports:

* `bsb_number` - Bank-State-Branch number of the bank account.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.bacs_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.bacs_debit`

The `payment_method_details.bacs_debit` attribute supports:

* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `sort_code` - Sort code of the bank account. (e.g., `10-20-30`)

<a id="payment_method_details.bancontact"></a>
### `payment_method_details.bancontact`

The `payment_method_details.bancontact` attribute supports:

* `bank_code` - Bank code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `bic` - Bank Identifier Code of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `generated_sepa_debit` - The ID of the SEPA Direct Debit PaymentMethod which was generated by this Charge.
* `generated_sepa_debit_mandate` - The mandate for the SEPA Direct Debit PaymentMethod which was generated by this Charge.
* `iban_last4` - Last four characters of the IBAN.
* `preferred_language` - Preferred language of the Bancontact authorization page that the customer is redirected to. Can be one of `en`, `de`, `fr`, or `nl` Possible values: `de`, `en`, `fr`, `nl`.
* `verified_name` - Owner's verified full name. Values are verified or provided by Bancontact directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.

<a id="payment_method_details.billie"></a>
### `payment_method_details.billie`

The `payment_method_details.billie` attribute supports:

* `transaction_id` - The Billie transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.bizum"></a>
### `payment_method_details.bizum`

The `payment_method_details.bizum` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.
* `transaction_id` - The Bizum transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.blik"></a>
### `payment_method_details.blik`

The `payment_method_details.blik` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique and immutable identifier assigned by BLIK to every buyer.

<a id="payment_method_details.boleto"></a>
### `payment_method_details.boleto`

The `payment_method_details.boleto` attribute supports:

* `tax_id` - The tax ID of the customer (CPF for individuals consumers or CNPJ for businesses consumers)

<a id="payment_method_details.card"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card`

The `payment_method_details.card` attribute supports:

* `amount_authorized` - The authorized amount.
* `authorization_code` - Authorization code on the charge.
* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `capture_before` - When using manual capture, a future timestamp at which the charge will be automatically refunded if uncaptured.
* `checks` - Check results by Card networks on Card address and CVC at time of payment. See [`payment_method_details.card.checks`](#payment_method_details.card.checks) below.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `electronic_commerce_indicator` - The Electronic Commerce Indicator (ECI) returned by the card network in the authorization response. Indicates the level of authentication used. Only populated for Visa and Mastercard transactions. This is the network's final ECI and can differ from the request value. An authenticated ECI alone doesn't determine liability shift.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `extended_authorization` - See [`payment_method_details.card.extended_authorization`](#payment_method_details.card.extended_authorization) below.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `incremental_authorization` - See [`payment_method_details.card.incremental_authorization`](#payment_method_details.card.incremental_authorization) below.
* `installments` - Installment details for this payment. For more information, see the [installments integration guide](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/installments). See [`payment_method_details.card.installments`](#payment_method_details.card.installments) below.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment or created by it.
* `multicapture` - See [`payment_method_details.card.multicapture`](#payment_method_details.card.multicapture) below.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.
* `network_token` - If this card has network token credentials, this contains the details of the network token credentials. See [`payment_method_details.card.network_token`](#payment_method_details.card.network_token) below.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `overcapture` - See [`payment_method_details.card.overcapture`](#payment_method_details.card.overcapture) below.
* `regulated_status` - Status of a card based on the card issuer. Possible values: `regulated`, `unregulated`.
* `three_d_secure` - Populated if this transaction used 3D Secure authentication. See [`payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure`](#payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure) below.
* `transaction_link_id` - Transaction Link ID (TLID) is a unique identifier for a transaction. This is used by some card networks, such as Mastercard, for transaction linking, in addition to Network Transaction IDs. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `wallet` - If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet. See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.checks"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.checks`

The `payment_method_details.card.checks` attribute supports:

* `address_line1_check` - If a address line1 was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.
* `address_postal_code_check` - If a address postal code was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.
* `cvc_check` - If a CVC was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.extended_authorization"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.extended_authorization`

The `payment_method_details.card.extended_authorization` attribute supports:

* `status` - Indicates whether or not the capture window is extended beyond the standard authorization. Possible values: `disabled`, `enabled`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.incremental_authorization"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.incremental_authorization`

The `payment_method_details.card.incremental_authorization` attribute supports:

* `status` - Indicates whether or not the incremental authorization feature is supported. Possible values: `available`, `unavailable`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.installments"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.installments`

The `payment_method_details.card.installments` attribute supports:

* `plan` - Installment plan selected for the payment. See [`payment_method_details.card.installments.plan`](#payment_method_details.card.installments.plan) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.installments.plan"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.installments.plan`

The `payment_method_details.card.installments.plan` attribute supports:

* `count` - For `fixed_count` installment plans, this is the number of installment payments your customer will make to their credit card.
* `interval` - For `fixed_count` installment plans, this is the interval between installment payments your customer will make to their credit card. One of `month`. Possible values: `month`.
* `type` - Type of installment plan, one of `fixed_count`, `bonus`, or `revolving`. Possible values: `bonus`, `fixed_count`, `revolving`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.multicapture"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.multicapture`

The `payment_method_details.card.multicapture` attribute supports:

* `status` - Indicates whether or not multiple captures are supported. Possible values: `available`, `unavailable`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.network_token"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.network_token`

The `payment_method_details.card.network_token` attribute supports:

* `used` - Indicates if Stripe used a network token, either user provided or Stripe managed when processing the transaction.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.overcapture"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.overcapture`

The `payment_method_details.card.overcapture` attribute supports:

* `maximum_amount_capturable` - The maximum amount that can be captured.
* `status` - Indicates whether or not the authorized amount can be over-captured. Possible values: `available`, `unavailable`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure`

The `payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure` attribute supports:

* `authentication_flow` - For authenticated transactions: how the customer was authenticated by the issuing bank. Possible values: `challenge`, `frictionless`.
* `electronic_commerce_indicator` - The Electronic Commerce Indicator (ECI). A protocol-level field indicating what degree of authentication was performed. Possible values: `01`, `02`, `05`, `06`, `07`.
* `exemption_indicator` - The exemption requested via 3DS and accepted by the issuer at authentication time. Possible values: `low_risk`, `none`.
* `exemption_indicator_applied` - Whether Stripe requested the value of `exemption_indicator` in the transaction. This will depend on the outcome of Stripe's internal risk assessment.
* `result` - Indicates the outcome of 3D Secure authentication. Possible values: `attempt_acknowledged`, `authenticated`, `data_share_only`, `exempted`, `failed`, `not_supported`, `processing_error`.
* `result_reason` - Additional information about why 3D Secure succeeded or failed based on the `result`. Possible values: `abandoned`, `bypassed`, `canceled`, `card_not_enrolled`, `network_not_supported`, `protocol_error`, `rejected`.
* `transaction_id` - The 3D Secure 1 XID or 3D Secure 2 Directory Server Transaction ID (dsTransId) for this payment.
* `version` - The version of 3D Secure that was used. Possible values: `1.0.2`, `2.1.0`, `2.2.0`, `2.3.0`, `2.3.1`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.wallet"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.wallet`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet` attribute supports:

* `dynamic_last4` - (For tokenized numbers only.) The last four digits of the device account number.
* `link` - See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.link`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.link) below.
* `masterpass` - See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass) below.
* `type` - The type of the card wallet, one of `amex_express_checkout`, `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `masterpass`, `samsung_pay`, `visa_checkout`, or `link`. An additional hash is included on the Wallet subhash with a name matching this value. It contains additional information specific to the card wallet type. Possible values: `amex_express_checkout`, `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `link`, `masterpass`, `samsung_pay`, `visa_checkout`.
* `visa_checkout` - See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.wallet.link"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.link`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet.link` attribute supports:

* `funding_source_group` - The [funding source group code](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/link-payment-methods) applied to this Link payment at confirmation time.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass` attribute supports:

* `billing_address` - Owner's verified billing address. Values are verified or provided by the wallet directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated. See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.billing_address`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.billing_address) below.
* `email` - Owner's verified email. Values are verified or provided by the wallet directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `name` - Owner's verified full name. Values are verified or provided by the wallet directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `shipping_address` - Owner's verified shipping address. Values are verified or provided by the wallet directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated. See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.shipping_address`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.shipping_address) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.billing_address"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.billing_address`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet.masterpass.billing_address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout`

They cannot be set or mutated. See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.billing_address`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.billing_address) below.
* `email` - Owner's verified email. Values are verified or provided by the wallet directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.

They cannot be set or mutated. See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.shipping_address`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.shipping_address) below.

### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.billing_address`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.billing_address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.shipping_address`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet.visa_checkout.shipping_address` attribute supports:

* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present`

The `payment_method_details.card_present` attribute supports:

* `amount_authorized` - The authorized amount
* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `brand_product` - The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.
* `capture_before` - When using manual capture, a future timestamp after which the charge will be automatically refunded if uncaptured.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `emv_auth_data` - Authorization response cryptogram.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_card` - ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.
* `incremental_authorization_supported` - Whether this [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents) is eligible for incremental authorizations. Request support using [request_incremental_authorization_support](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-payment_method_options-card_present-request_incremental_authorization_support).
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `offline` - Details about payments collected offline. See [`payment_method_details.card_present.offline`](#payment_method_details.card_present.offline) below.
* `overcapture_supported` - Defines whether the authorized amount can be over-captured or not
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `receipt` - A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions. See [`payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`](#payment_method_details.card_present.receipt) below.
* `wallet` - See [`payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`](#payment_method_details.card_present.wallet) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present.offline"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present.offline`

The `payment_method_details.card_present.offline` attribute supports:

* `stored_at` - Time at which the payment was collected while offline
* `type` - The method used to process this payment method offline. Only deferred is allowed. Possible values: `deferred`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present.receipt"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`

The `payment_method_details.card_present.receipt` attribute supports:

* `account_type` - The type of account being debited or credited Possible values: `checking`, `credit`, `prepaid`, `unknown`.
* `application_cryptogram` - The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.
* `application_preferred_name` - The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `authorization_code` - Identifier for this transaction.
* `authorization_response_code` - EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.
* `cardholder_verification_method` - Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.
* `dedicated_file_name` - Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.
* `terminal_verification_results` - A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.
* `transaction_status_information` - An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present.wallet"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`

The `payment_method_details.card_present.wallet` attribute supports:

* `type` - The type of mobile wallet, one of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, or `unknown`. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, `unknown`.

<a id="payment_method_details.cashapp"></a>
### `payment_method_details.cashapp`

The `payment_method_details.cashapp` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique and immutable identifier assigned by Cash App to every buyer.
* `cashtag` - A public identifier for buyers using Cash App.
* `transaction_id` - A unique and immutable identifier of payments assigned by Cash App

<a id="payment_method_details.crypto"></a>
### `payment_method_details.crypto`

The `payment_method_details.crypto` attribute supports:

* `buyer_address` - The wallet address of the customer.
* `network` - The blockchain network that the transaction was sent on. Possible values: `base`, `ethereum`, `polygon`, `solana`, `sui`, `tempo`.
* `token_currency` - The token currency that the transaction was sent with. Possible values: `phantom_cash`, `usdc`, `usdg`, `usdp`, `usdsui`, `usdt`.
* `transaction_hash` - The blockchain transaction hash of the crypto payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.eps"></a>
### `payment_method_details.eps`

The `payment_method_details.eps` attribute supports:

* `bank` - The customer's bank. <a id="payment_method_details.interac_present"></a>
### `payment_method_details.interac_present`

The `payment_method_details.interac_present` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `interac`, `mastercard` or `visa`.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `emv_auth_data` - Authorization response cryptogram.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_card` - ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `receipt` - A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions. See [`payment_method_details.interac_present.receipt`](#payment_method_details.interac_present.receipt) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.interac_present.receipt"></a>
### `payment_method_details.interac_present.receipt`

The `payment_method_details.interac_present.receipt` attribute supports:

* `account_type` - The type of account being debited or credited Possible values: `checking`, `savings`, `unknown`.
* `application_cryptogram` - The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.
* `application_preferred_name` - The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `authorization_code` - Identifier for this transaction.
* `authorization_response_code` - EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.
* `cardholder_verification_method` - Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.
* `dedicated_file_name` - Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.
* `terminal_verification_results` - A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.
* `transaction_status_information` - An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.

### `payment_method_details.sunbit`

The `payment_method_details.sunbit` attribute supports:

* `transaction_id` - The Sunbit transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.swish"></a>
### `payment_method_details.swish`

The `payment_method_details.swish` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies the payer's Swish account. You can use this attribute to check whether two Swish transactions were paid for by the same payer
* `payment_reference` - Payer bank reference number for the payment
* `verified_phone_last4` - The last four digits of the Swish account phone number

<a id="payment_method_details.twint"></a>
### `payment_method_details.twint`

The `payment_method_details.twint` attribute supports:

* `mandate` - ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent.

<a id="payment_method_details.upi"></a>
### `payment_method_details.upi`

The `payment_method_details.upi` attribute supports:

* `vpa` - Customer's unique Virtual Payment Address.

<a id="payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `payment_reference` - Reference number to locate ACH payments with customer's bank.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="payment_method_details.wechat_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.wechat_pay`

The `payment_method_details.wechat_pay` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular WeChat Pay account. You can use this attribute to check whether two WeChat accounts are the same.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `transaction_id` - Transaction ID of this particular WeChat Pay transaction.

<a id="presentment_details"></a>
### `presentment_details`

The `presentment_details` attribute supports:

* `presentment_amount` - Amount intended to be collected by this payment, denominated in `presentment_currency`.
* `presentment_currency` - Currency presented to the customer during payment.

<a id="radar_options"></a>
### `radar_options`

The `radar_options` attribute supports:

* `session` - A [Radar Session](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/radar-session) is a snapshot of the browser metadata and device details that help Radar make more accurate predictions on your payments.

<a id="refunds"></a>
### `refunds`

The `refunds` attribute supports:

* `data` - Details about each object. See [`refunds.data`](#refunds.data) below.
* `has_more` - True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`. Possible values: `list`.
* `url` - The URL where this list can be accessed.

<a id="refunds.data"></a>
### `refunds.data`

The `refunds.data` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `balance_transaction` - Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.
* `charge` - ID of the charge that's refunded.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `customer` - ID of the customer of this refund.
* `customer_account` - ID of the account of this refund.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. You can use this for displaying to users (available on non-card refunds only).
* `destination_details` - See [`refunds.data.destination_details`](#refunds.data.destination_details) below.
* `failure_balance_transaction` - After the refund fails, this balance transaction describes the adjustment made on your account balance that reverses the initial balance transaction.
* `failure_reason` - Provides the reason for the refund failure. Possible values are: `lost_or_stolen_card`, `expired_or_canceled_card`, `charge_for_pending_refund_disputed`, `insufficient_funds`, `declined`, `merchant_request`, or `unknown`.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `instructions_email` - For payment methods without native refund support (for example, Konbini, PromptPay), provide an email address for the customer to receive refund instructions.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `next_action` - See [`refunds.data.next_action`](#refunds.data.next_action) below.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `refund`.
* `payment_intent` - ID of the PaymentIntent that's refunded.
* `payment_method` - ID of the payment method associated with this refund.
* `pending_reason` - Provides the reason for why the refund is pending. Possible values are: `processing`, `insufficient_funds`, or `charge_pending`. Possible values: `charge_pending`, `insufficient_funds`, `processing`.
* `presentment_details` - See [`refunds.data.presentment_details`](#refunds.data.presentment_details) below.
* `reason` - Reason for the refund, which is either user-provided (`duplicate`, `fraudulent`, or `requested_by_customer`) or generated by Stripe internally (`expired_uncaptured_charge`). Possible values: `duplicate`, `expired_uncaptured_charge`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`.
* `receipt_number` - This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this refund.
* `source_transfer_reversal` - The transfer reversal that's associated with the refund. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account.
* `status` - Status of the refund. This can be `pending`, `requires_action`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`. Learn more about [failed refunds](https://docs.stripe.com/refunds#failed-refunds).
* `transfer_reversal` - This refers to the transfer reversal object if the accompanying transfer reverses. This is only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter.

* `swish` - See [`refunds.data.destination_details.swish`](#refunds.data.destination_details.swish) below.
* `th_bank_transfer` - See [`refunds.data.destination_details.th_bank_transfer`](#refunds.data.destination_details.th_bank_transfer) below.
* `type` - The type of transaction-specific details of the payment method used in the refund (e.g., `card`). An additional hash is included on `destination_details` with a name matching this value. It contains information specific to the refund transaction.
* `us_bank_transfer` - See [`refunds.data.destination_details.us_bank_transfer`](#refunds.data.destination_details.us_bank_transfer) below.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a charge whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_charge.deposit

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_charge.deposit
```

The charge stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a charge using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_charge.deposit
  id = "ch_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_charge.deposit
  identity = {
    id = "ch_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the charge.

Using `terraform import`, import a charge using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_charge.deposit ch_123
```

-> Stripe does not return `source` as it was sent, or `capture`, so an imported charge has them null. Leave them out of its configuration: changing either needs a new charge.
